_comment: Proposed rewrites fed to the real grounding checks. One per ref, because grounding takes the first rewrite it sees for a line. `expect` is a note to the reader — the runner prints the real outcome beside it, and where they disagree the code is right.
request: Tailor my resume to the Northwind payments posting

changes.expect: kept — adds only PostgreSQL, which the resume already shows
changes.text: Backend engineer with six years building payment and billing services in Python and PostgreSQL. Comfortable owning a service end to end, from schema design to on-call.
changes.reason: Leads with the stack the posting asks for

changes.expect: dropped — Kubernetes appears nowhere on the resume
changes.text: Built Python services for checkout and refunds on Kubernetes that cut median latency 30%

changes.expect: kept, with the invented 500 blanked to [__]
changes.text: Tuned PostgreSQL queries and added partial indexes so the billing API absorbed 2x traffic across 500 services without new hardware

changes.expect: ignored — identical to the line already there
changes.text: Led the migration from nightly batch settlement to an event-driven pipeline, cutting reconciliation time from 6 hours to 20 minutes

changes.expect: refused — the rewrite would lose the 12 the line already states
changes.text: Shared on-call and wrote the runbooks the team still uses

changes.expect: dropped — appends 'enhancing operational efficiency', an outcome the resume never claims. Verbatim from a live GPT-4o run.
changes.text: Developed Django REST services for an inventory product utilized by 40 warehouse teams, enhancing operational efficiency.

changes.expect: dropped — 'though exact numbers are not specified' is commentary about the resume, not a resume line. Verbatim from a live GPT-4o run.
changes.text: Implemented a validated pipeline to replace a hand-rolled CSV importer, reducing support tickets by half, though exact numbers are not specified.

changes.expect: kept — ordinary rewording is allowed; the checks police named things, invented outcomes and commentary, not vocabulary
